## COMPREHENSIVE SHORING AND SCAFFOLDING PLAN - LEVEL 2 SUSPENDED SLAB
*   **Document Title:** Level 2 Suspended Slab Shoring Plan & Details
*   **Contact:** TEL. 778 898 5301, Email: info@ttfscaffolding.com (TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. contact, likely acting as a sub-consultant or supplier providing engineering support)
*   **Shoring Equipment Supplier:** TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd.
*   **Scales:** As Shown (Refer to specific plan views for detailed scales, primarily 1/8” = 1’-0” for overall plans).
*   **Project Name:** Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition
*   **Project Location:** 10441 - 132 Street, Surrey, British Columbia, Canada
*   **General Contractor:** (To be specified by project management)

*   **Scope of Work:** This document details the shoring and scaffolding requirements for the Level 2 Suspended Slab and associated structural elements (beams, slab bands) at the Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition project. It outlines the specific layout, material specifications, load capacities, and installation guidelines necessary to safely support the concrete structure during its curing period.

2.1 **Drawing Coordination:** This drawing shall be read in conjunction with, and is supplemental to, the latest architectural, structural, and mechanical drawings for the Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition project. Any discrepancies or conflicts between these drawings shall be brought to the immediate attention of the Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) and the General Contractor for clarification prior to commencing any work.

2.2 **Field Verification:** The Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.) is solely responsible for checking and confirming all dimensions, elevations, and existing site conditions prior to the shipment of shoring equipment and commencement of installation. Any deviations from the dimensions or conditions shown on this drawing must be reported to the P. Eng. for review and approval before proceeding.

2.3 **Professional Engineering Oversight:** All shoring and scaffolding installations must be performed under the direct supervision of qualified personnel and in strict accordance with this plan and all applicable safety regulations. An inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is mandatory prior to the pouring of concrete. A minimum of forty-eight (48) hours' notice is required for scheduling this inspection.

2.4 **Material Usage Restrictions:** All 4-inch by 6-inch (4x6) wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically designated for their intended structural purpose as joists within the shoring system. These joists shall NOT be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purposes unless explicitly approved in writing by the Professional Engineer. Misuse of these materials can compromise the structural integrity of the shoring system.

3.1 **Purpose:** The shoring system detailed herein is designed to provide temporary vertical support for the freshly placed concrete of the Level 2 suspended slab, slab bands, and reinforced concrete beams until the concrete has achieved sufficient strength to be self-supporting, as determined by the structural engineer.
3.2 **Key Components:** The shoring system primarily consists of:
*   **Heavy-Duty Shoring Frames:** Modular steel frames, typically stacked, providing primary vertical support.
*   **Adjustable Post Shores:** Individual steel posts with adjustable height mechanisms, used for specific point loads or areas requiring localized support.
*   **Wood Joists:** Dimensional lumber (4x6) spanning between shoring frames or post shores to support the plywood decking.
*   **Plywood Decking:** Structural plywood forming the soffit (bottom surface) of the concrete slab.
*   **Adjustable Screw Jacks:** Base plates with threaded rods for fine height adjustment at the bottom of shoring frames and post shores.
*   **Adjustable U-Head Plates:** Top plates with U-shaped heads for supporting wood joists at the top of shoring frames and post shores, allowing for fine height adjustment.
*   **Bracing:** Diagonal and horizontal bracing elements for shoring frames to ensure stability and resist lateral loads.

*   **Build-Up Materials:** Temporary structural elements (e.g., timber cribbing, steel beams) provided by the contractor to achieve required elevations under specific conditions, such as sloped areas or where the ground/supporting structure is not level.
*   **Typical Suspended Slab:** The Level 2 suspended slab has a typical thickness of 10.5 inches (ten and one-half inches), unless otherwise noted (U.N.O.).

*   **Typical Slab Band:** Integrated within the slab, typical slab bands have a depth of 24 inches (twenty-four inches), U.N.O. Slab bands are thickened portions of the slab, acting as shallow beams to carry heavier loads or span longer distances.

*   **300x450 DP. R/C BEAM:** Reinforced concrete beams with nominal dimensions of 300 millimeters (11.81 inches) in width and 450 millimeters (17.72 inches) in depth. These beams require specific shoring support due to their concentrated loads.

*   **300x500 DP. R/C BEAM:** Reinforced concrete beams with nominal dimensions of 300 millimeters (11.81 inches) in width and 500 millimeters (19.69 inches) in depth. These beams are deeper and typically carry higher loads, thus requiring robust shoring.
The shoring system has been designed to safely support the following loads, including the weight of wet concrete, formwork, construction live loads, and any temporary equipment.

*   **10.5” Deep Slab:** Designed for a minimum uniform distributed load capacity of 182 pounds per square foot (PSF). This value accounts for the self-weight of the 10.5-inch thick wet concrete, formwork, and a specified construction live load.

*   **24” Deep Slab Band:** Designed for a minimum uniform distributed load capacity of 350 pounds per square foot (PSF). This higher value accommodates the increased self-weight of the deeper concrete section, formwork, and associated construction live loads.

*   **Heavy Duty Frames:** All shoring frames specified are heavy-duty steel frames, each designed with a minimum vertical load capacity of 10 kips (10,000 pounds) per leg. This capacity applies to each individual vertical standard (leg) of the frame system. The total capacity of a frame assembly will depend on the number of legs and configuration.
*   **#2 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by an 'X' symbol.
*   **#3 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by a '[X]' symbol.
*   **#4 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by an '&' symbol.

*   *Note:* The exact load capacity for each type of post shore (#2, #3, #4) is dependent on its extended height and manufacturer specifications. The contractor shall ensure that the selected post shores meet or exceed the required design loads for their specific locations.
All materials used in the shoring system must meet the specified grades and standards to ensure the structural integrity and safety of the temporary works.

*   **Grade:** Douglas Fir (D. FIR) #1 or better. This specifies a high-grade structural plywood suitable for concrete formwork, offering excellent strength and durability. Plywood shall be free from defects that could impair its strength or finish quality.
*   **Source:** Supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. This ensures consistency in material quality and adherence to specified structural properties.
*   **Grade:** Heavy-duty structural grade lumber, free from significant knots, splits, or other defects that would reduce its load-carrying capacity.
*   **Purpose:** These joists are specifically intended to span between shoring frames or post shores to support the plywood decking and transfer the slab loads to the vertical supports.
*   **Restriction:** As per Section 2.4, these joists shall NOT be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purposes.

*   **Dimensions:** Each frame unit is 5 feet (5'-0") high by 4 feet (4'-0") wide. For required heights, frames are typically stacked, e.g., two 5-foot frames stacked for a total height of 10 feet (5'+5' HIGH).
*   **Capacity:** Each leg of the frame assembly must be capable of supporting a minimum of 10 kips (10,000 pounds).

*   **Bracing:** Frames shall be braced using 7-foot (7'-0") long diagonal or horizontal bracing elements, typical unless otherwise noted (TYP. U.N.O.). Bracing is crucial for lateral stability and overall system rigidity.
*   **Manufacturer:** To be supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. or an approved equivalent.

*   **Certification:** Post shores must be certified by the manufacturer for their stated load capacities at various extended heights, in accordance with applicable safety standards (e.g., CSA S269.1, OSHA).
*   **Purpose:** Used at the bottom of shoring frames and post shores to provide fine vertical adjustment, ensure level bearing, and distribute loads to the supporting surface.
*   **Requirement:** Required for all 4-foot (4'-0") high frames and post shores at their base.
*   **Material:** Heavy-duty steel construction with robust threading.
*   **Purpose:** Used at the top of shoring frames and post shores to provide fine vertical adjustment and create a stable saddle for supporting the wood joists.
*   **Requirement:** Required for all 4-foot (4'-0") high frames and post shores at their top.
*   **Material:** Heavy-duty steel construction with a U-shaped head to cradle the joists and robust threading for adjustment.

*   **Purpose:** Temporary structural elements required to achieve specified shoring elevations where the supporting surface is uneven, sloped, or at a significantly lower elevation than the shoring base. This includes "BUILD UP UNDER SLAB" and "BUILD UP UNDER SLOPE FOR STAIRS."
*   **Responsibility:** The selection, design, and installation of these build-up materials are the sole responsibility of the Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.).

*   **Materials:** Typically consists of engineered lumber, heavy timber cribbing, or structural steel sections. All build-up materials must be structurally sound, adequately sized, and properly installed to safely transfer loads to the underlying support. The contractor must submit their build-up plan to the P. Eng. for review and approval if not explicitly detailed on the drawings.
All dimensions are in feet and inches unless otherwise specified.
*   The plan view delineates the general arrangement of shoring frames and post shores. Specific areas are identified for different shoring requirements.

*   **General Bay Spacing:** The shoring system is organized into bays with typical dimensions of 10'-6" (ten feet, six inches) in one direction, and varying dimensions in the perpendicular direction, including 16' (sixteen feet), 14' (fourteen feet), and 20' (twenty feet).
*   Multiple sections indicate bay dimensions of 10'-6" (three consecutive bays).
*   Perpendicular to these, bays are indicated with dimensions such as 16', 14', 14', 14', 14', 20'.
*   A specific section indicates 40'-6" (forty feet, six inches) and 40'-6" lengths, with a 5'-0" (five feet, zero inches) width.

*   **On-Center Spacing:** Wood joists (4x6) are to be spaced at 19.2 inches (19.2") on center (O/C). This spacing is critical for distributing the slab load effectively to the supporting shoring frames or post shores without overstressing the plywood decking. This spacing is typical for the main slab areas and specifically noted "under step" and "under slab."
*   **Quantity:** A note indicates "12 pcs." (twelve pieces) at 19.2" O/C, likely referring to a specific section or typical number of joists required for a given bay width.
*   Post shores are required ONLY where explicitly shown or marked on the plan.
*   **No Shoring Default:** No shoring is required under the typical 10.5" slab nor under the 24" slab band unless specifically indicated.
*   **'X' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #2 Post Shore.
*   **'[X]' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #3 Post Shore.
*   **'&' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #4 Post Shore.
*   The contractor must refer to the plan for the precise location of each post shore type.

*   **EL. 89.95m:** This elevation indicates a specific point on the shoring plan, likely the top of the shoring structure or a key datum point, at 89.95 meters above the established project datum. This metric elevation should be carefully cross-referenced with architectural and structural drawings to ensure consistency with the overall project elevation scheme.
*   All shoring equipment shall be installed plumb, level, and true to the dimensions and elevations shown on this drawing.
*   The entire shoring system must be stable and adequately braced before any concrete placement.
*   Ensure all connections, pins, and locking devices on shoring frames and post shores are properly engaged and secured.
*   Stack 5-foot (5'-0") high frames as required to achieve the necessary shoring height, ensuring proper alignment and secure pin connections between stacked frames.

*   Install 7-foot (7'-0") bracing diagonally or horizontally between frames to create a rigid and stable tower or wall system. Bracing must be installed at all levels and in both directions to resist lateral loads.
*   Ensure all frames are equipped with adjustable screw jacks at the base and adjustable U-head plates at the top, as specified.
*   Place #2, #3, or #4 post shores precisely at the locations marked with 'X', '[X]', or '&' symbols, respectively, on the shoring plan.
*   Ensure post shores are plumb and have full bearing on the supporting surface below.
*   Utilize screw jack base plates at the bottom and U-head plates at the top for fine height adjustment and proper load transfer.
*   Adjust post shores to the exact required elevation to support the formwork.
*   Lay 4x6 wood joists at 19.2 inches on center (O/C) across the U-head plates of the shoring frames and post shores. Ensure joists are level and securely seated within the U-heads.

*   Place 3/4-inch Douglas Fir #1 plywood decking on top of the joists, ensuring a tight fit and smooth surface for the concrete pour. Secure plywood as necessary to prevent displacement during concrete placement.
*   Screw jack base plates and U-head plates are to be used for final height adjustment and to compensate for minor variations in the supporting surface or formwork.
*   Adjustments should be made carefully to ensure uniform load distribution across all shoring elements. Avoid over-tightening any single jack, which could induce uneven stresses.

*   The Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.) is responsible for designing and installing all "BUILD UP UNDER SLAB" and "BUILD UP UNDER SLOPE FOR STAIRS" as required to achieve the specified shoring elevations.

*   These build-up elements must be structurally sound and capable of safely transferring the shoring loads to the underlying structure or ground. Detailed shop drawings or a specific design by the contractor's engineer may be required for complex build-up scenarios.

*   A critical instruction is that **NO SHORE IS REQUIRED UNDER THE TYPICAL 10.5" SLAB NOR UNDER THE 24" SLAB BAND TYPICALLY**, unless specifically indicated on the plan with an 'X', '[X]', or '&' symbol for post shores. This implies that the main shoring frames and joists are primarily supporting the overall slab area, and specific post shores are only needed for localized heavy loads or complex geometry not covered by the general frame layout. The contractor must strictly adhere to this instruction to avoid unnecessary installation or, conversely, missing critical support.

*   A mandatory inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is required prior to pouring concrete. This inspection will verify that the shoring system has been installed in full compliance with this drawing, engineering calculations, and all applicable safety standards.

*   The Shoring/Forming Contractor must provide a minimum of forty-eight (48) hours' notice to the P. Eng. to schedule this inspection. No concrete shall be placed until written approval is received from the P. Eng.
*   The Contractor must ensure that all field personnel are familiar with the contents of this drawing and all referenced documents.

*   Continuous field verification of dimensions, elevations, and material conditions is required throughout the installation process. Any discrepancies or unforeseen conditions must be immediately reported to the P. Eng.
*   Strict adherence to the restriction on 4x6 wood joist usage (Section 2.4) is paramount for safety. Misuse of these structural members can lead to catastrophic failure of the shoring system.

*   All work shall be performed in accordance with the latest edition of the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations (OHSR) of British Columbia, Canada, and the Contractor's site-specific safety plan.
*   Personnel working on or near the shoring system must wear appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
*   Proper fall protection measures must be in place during the erection and dismantling of the shoring and formwork.
*   Access and egress points must be kept clear.
*   The shoring system must be protected from accidental impact by vehicles or equipment.
*   Regular inspection of the shoring system for signs of damage, settlement, or instability is required, especially after adverse weather conditions or before concrete placement.

*   Greuter Engineering Ltd., under EGBC Permit No. 1002364, is the Engineer of Record for this shoring design. The P. Eng. is responsible for the overall design integrity and approval of the shoring plan.
*   The P. Eng. will conduct the pre-pour inspection to confirm compliance with the design.
*   All materials, including steel frames, post shores, wood joists, and plywood, must meet or exceed the specifications outlined in Section 5.0.

*   The Shoring/Forming Contractor is responsible for ensuring that all supplied materials are in good condition, free from damage, corrosion, or defects that could impair their structural performance.
*   Manufacturer's certifications and data sheets for proprietary shoring equipment (frames, post shores, jacks) shall be available on site for review.

## COMPREHENSIVE SHORING AND SCAFFOLDING PLAN - LEVEL 2 SUSPENDED SLAB

**Document Control Information:**

*   **Document Title:** Level 2 Suspended Slab Shoring Plan & Details
*   **Drawing Number:** F-2
*   **Date of Issue:** November 04, 2025
*   **Revision Date:** November 12, 2025 (Initial Revision)
*   **Prepared By:** F.T. (Drafter)
*   **Engineering Firm:** Greuter Engineering Ltd.
    *   **EGBC Permit No.:** 1002364
    *   **Project File No.:** GE-3548-1
    *   **Contact:** TEL. 778 898 5301, Email: info@ttfscaffolding.com (TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. contact, likely acting as a sub-consultant or supplier providing engineering support)
*   **Shoring Equipment Supplier:** TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd.
    *   **Website:** www.ttfscaffolding.com
*   **Scales:** As Shown (Refer to specific plan views for detailed scales, primarily 1/8” = 1’-0” for overall plans).

---

### 1.0 PROJECT INFORMATION

*   **Project Name:** Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition
*   **Project Location:** 10441 - 132 Street, Surrey, British Columbia, Canada
*   **General Contractor:** (To be specified by project management)
*   **Shoring / Forming Contractor:** DC Forming Ltd.
*   **Scope of Work:** This document details the shoring and scaffolding requirements for the Level 2 Suspended Slab and associated structural elements (beams, slab bands) at the Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition project. It outlines the specific layout, material specifications, load capacities, and installation guidelines necessary to safely support the concrete structure during its curing period.

---

### 2.0 GENERAL NOTES AND DISCLAIMERS

2.1 **Drawing Coordination:** This drawing shall be read in conjunction with, and is supplemental to, the latest architectural, structural, and mechanical drawings for the Kwantlen Park Secondary School Addition project. Any discrepancies or conflicts between these drawings shall be brought to the immediate attention of the Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) and the General Contractor for clarification prior to commencing any work.

2.2 **Field Verification:** The Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.) is solely responsible for checking and confirming all dimensions, elevations, and existing site conditions prior to the shipment of shoring equipment and commencement of installation. Any deviations from the dimensions or conditions shown on this drawing must be reported to the P. Eng. for review and approval before proceeding.

2.3 **Professional Engineering Oversight:** All shoring and scaffolding installations must be performed under the direct supervision of qualified personnel and in strict accordance with this plan and all applicable safety regulations. An inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is mandatory prior to the pouring of concrete. A minimum of forty-eight (48) hours' notice is required for scheduling this inspection.

2.4 **Material Usage Restrictions:** All 4-inch by 6-inch (4x6) wood joists supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. are specifically designated for their intended structural purpose as joists within the shoring system. These joists shall NOT be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purposes unless explicitly approved in writing by the Professional Engineer. Misuse of these materials can compromise the structural integrity of the shoring system.

---

### 3.0 STRUCTURAL SYSTEM OVERVIEW

3.1 **Purpose:** The shoring system detailed herein is designed to provide temporary vertical support for the freshly placed concrete of the Level 2 suspended slab, slab bands, and reinforced concrete beams until the concrete has achieved sufficient strength to be self-supporting, as determined by the structural engineer.

3.2 **Key Components:** The shoring system primarily consists of:
    *   **Heavy-Duty Shoring Frames:** Modular steel frames, typically stacked, providing primary vertical support.
    *   **Adjustable Post Shores:** Individual steel posts with adjustable height mechanisms, used for specific point loads or areas requiring localized support.
    *   **Wood Joists:** Dimensional lumber (4x6) spanning between shoring frames or post shores to support the plywood decking.
    *   **Plywood Decking:** Structural plywood forming the soffit (bottom surface) of the concrete slab.
    *   **Adjustable Screw Jacks:** Base plates with threaded rods for fine height adjustment at the bottom of shoring frames and post shores.
    *   **Adjustable U-Head Plates:** Top plates with U-shaped heads for supporting wood joists at the top of shoring frames and post shores, allowing for fine height adjustment.
    *   **Bracing:** Diagonal and horizontal bracing elements for shoring frames to ensure stability and resist lateral loads.
    *   **Build-Up Materials:** Temporary structural elements (e.g., timber cribbing, steel beams) provided by the contractor to achieve required elevations under specific conditions, such as sloped areas or where the ground/supporting structure is not level.

3.3 **Slab and Beam Details:**
    *   **Typical Suspended Slab:** The Level 2 suspended slab has a typical thickness of 10.5 inches (ten and one-half inches), unless otherwise noted (U.N.O.).
    *   **Typical Slab Band:** Integrated within the slab, typical slab bands have a depth of 24 inches (twenty-four inches), U.N.O. Slab bands are thickened portions of the slab, acting as shallow beams to carry heavier loads or span longer distances.
    *   **Reinforced Concrete Beams (R/C Beams):**
        *   **300x450 DP. R/C BEAM:** Reinforced concrete beams with nominal dimensions of 300 millimeters (11.81 inches) in width and 450 millimeters (17.72 inches) in depth. These beams require specific shoring support due to their concentrated loads.
        *   **300x500 DP. R/C BEAM:** Reinforced concrete beams with nominal dimensions of 300 millimeters (11.81 inches) in width and 500 millimeters (19.69 inches) in depth. These beams are deeper and typically carry higher loads, thus requiring robust shoring.

---

### 4.0 LOAD SPECIFICATIONS AND DESIGN CRITERIA

The shoring system has been designed to safely support the following loads, including the weight of wet concrete, formwork, construction live loads, and any temporary equipment.

4.1 **Slab Design Loads:**
    *   **10.5” Deep Slab:** Designed for a minimum uniform distributed load capacity of 182 pounds per square foot (PSF). This value accounts for the self-weight of the 10.5-inch thick wet concrete, formwork, and a specified construction live load.
    *   **24” Deep Slab Band:** Designed for a minimum uniform distributed load capacity of 350 pounds per square foot (PSF). This higher value accommodates the increased self-weight of the deeper concrete section, formwork, and associated construction live loads.

4.2 **Shoring Frame Capacity:**
    *   **Heavy Duty Frames:** All shoring frames specified are heavy-duty steel frames, each designed with a minimum vertical load capacity of 10 kips (10,000 pounds) per leg. This capacity applies to each individual vertical standard (leg) of the frame system. The total capacity of a frame assembly will depend on the number of legs and configuration.

4.3 **Post Shore Capacity:**
    *   **#2 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by an 'X' symbol.
    *   **#3 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by a '[X]' symbol.
    *   **#4 Post Shore:** Specific capacity to be verified with manufacturer's data sheets. Used for localized support as indicated on the plan by an '&' symbol.
    *   *Note:* The exact load capacity for each type of post shore (#2, #3, #4) is dependent on its extended height and manufacturer specifications. The contractor shall ensure that the selected post shores meet or exceed the required design loads for their specific locations.

---

### 5.0 MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS AND SPECIFICATIONS

All materials used in the shoring system must meet the specified grades and standards to ensure the structural integrity and safety of the temporary works.

5.1 **Plywood Decking:**
    *   **Type:** Minimum 3/4-inch (0.75") thick structural plywood.
    *   **Grade:** Douglas Fir (D. FIR) #1 or better. This specifies a high-grade structural plywood suitable for concrete formwork, offering excellent strength and durability. Plywood shall be free from defects that could impair its strength or finish quality.

5.2 **Wood Joists:**
    *   **Type:** 4-inch by 6-inch (4x6) dimensional lumber joists.
    *   **Source:** Supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. This ensures consistency in material quality and adherence to specified structural properties.
    *   **Grade:** Heavy-duty structural grade lumber, free from significant knots, splits, or other defects that would reduce its load-carrying capacity.
    *   **Purpose:** These joists are specifically intended to span between shoring frames or post shores to support the plywood decking and transfer the slab loads to the vertical supports.
    *   **Restriction:** As per Section 2.4, these joists shall NOT be used for packing, blocking, shims, or cut short for any other purposes.

5.3 **Shoring Frames:**
    *   **Type:** Heavy-duty modular steel shoring frames.
    *   **Dimensions:** Each frame unit is 5 feet (5'-0") high by 4 feet (4'-0") wide. For required heights, frames are typically stacked, e.g., two 5-foot frames stacked for a total height of 10 feet (5'+5' HIGH).
    *   **Capacity:** Each leg of the frame assembly must be capable of supporting a minimum of 10 kips (10,000 pounds).
    *   **Bracing:** Frames shall be braced using 7-foot (7'-0") long diagonal or horizontal bracing elements, typical unless otherwise noted (TYP. U.N.O.). Bracing is crucial for lateral stability and overall system rigidity.

5.4 **Post Shores:**
    *   **Types:** #2, #3, and #4 adjustable steel post shores.
    *   **Manufacturer:** To be supplied by TTF Scaffolding Co. Ltd. or an approved equivalent.
    *   **Certification:** Post shores must be certified by the manufacturer for their stated load capacities at various extended heights, in accordance with applicable safety standards (e.g., CSA S269.1, OSHA).

5.5 **Adjustable Screw Jacks (Base Plates):**
    *   **Purpose:** Used at the bottom of shoring frames and post shores to provide fine vertical adjustment, ensure level bearing, and distribute loads to the supporting surface.
    *   **Requirement:** Required for all 4-foot (4'-0") high frames and post shores at their base.
    *   **Material:** Heavy-duty steel construction with robust threading.

5.6 **Adjustable U-Head Plates (Top Plates):**
    *   **Purpose:** Used at the top of shoring frames and post shores to provide fine vertical adjustment and create a stable saddle for supporting the wood joists.
    *   **Requirement:** Required for all 4-foot (4'-0") high frames and post shores at their top.
    *   **Material:** Heavy-duty steel construction with a U-shaped head to cradle the joists and robust threading for adjustment.

5.7 **Build-Up Materials (By Contractor):**
    *   **Purpose:** Temporary structural elements required to achieve specified shoring elevations where the supporting surface is uneven, sloped, or at a significantly lower elevation than the shoring base. This includes "BUILD UP UNDER SLAB" and "BUILD UP UNDER SLOPE FOR STAIRS."
    *   **Responsibility:** The selection, design, and installation of these build-up materials are the sole responsibility of the Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.).
    *   **Materials:** Typically consists of engineered lumber, heavy timber cribbing, or structural steel sections. All build-up materials must be structurally sound, adequately sized, and properly installed to safely transfer loads to the underlying support. The contractor must submit their build-up plan to the P. Eng. for review and approval if not explicitly detailed on the drawings.

---

### 6.0 DIMENSIONS, LAYOUT, AND ELEVATIONS

All dimensions are in feet and inches unless otherwise specified.

6.1 **Overall Shoring Plan Layout (Level 2 Suspended Slab):**
    *   The plan view delineates the general arrangement of shoring frames and post shores. Specific areas are identified for different shoring requirements.
    *   **General Bay Spacing:** The shoring system is organized into bays with typical dimensions of 10'-6" (ten feet, six inches) in one direction, and varying dimensions in the perpendicular direction, including 16' (sixteen feet), 14' (fourteen feet), and 20' (twenty feet).
    *   **Specific Bay Dimensions:**
        *   Multiple sections indicate bay dimensions of 10'-6" (three consecutive bays).
        *   Perpendicular to these, bays are indicated with dimensions such as 16', 14', 14', 14', 14', 20'.
        *   Other areas show 16', 14', 10'-6" and 16', 14', 44' (forty-four feet).
        *   A specific section indicates 40'-6" (forty feet, six inches) and 40'-6" lengths, with a 5'-0" (five feet, zero inches) width.
        *   Additional dimensions include 10', 16', 14', 16', and 14', 9'.

6.2 **Wood Joist Spacing and Length:**
    *   **Joist Length:** 12 feet (12'-0") for typical applications.
    *   **On-Center Spacing:** Wood joists (4x6) are to be spaced at 19.2 inches (19.2") on center (O/C). This spacing is critical for distributing the slab load effectively to the supporting shoring frames or post shores without overstressing the plywood decking. This spacing is typical for the main slab areas and specifically noted "under step" and "under slab."
    *   **Quantity:** A note indicates "12 pcs." (twelve pieces) at 19.2" O/C, likely referring to a specific section or typical number of joists required for a given bay width.

6.3 **Post Shore Locations:**
    *   Post shores are required ONLY where explicitly shown or marked on the plan.
    *   **No Shoring Default:** No shoring is required under the typical 10.5" slab nor under the 24" slab band unless specifically indicated.
    *   **Designation Symbols:**
        *   **'X' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #2 Post Shore.
        *   **'[X]' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #3 Post Shore.
        *   **'&' Symbol:** Indicates the location for a #4 Post Shore.
    *   The contractor must refer to the plan for the precise location of each post shore type.

6.4 **Elevations:**
    *   **EL. 89.95m:** This elevation indicates a specific point on the shoring plan, likely the top of the shoring structure or a key datum point, at 89.95 meters above the established project datum. This metric elevation should be carefully cross-referenced with architectural and structural drawings to ensure consistency with the overall project elevation scheme.

---

### 7.0 INSTALLATION PROCEDURES AND REQUIREMENTS

7.1 **General Installation Guidance:**
    *   All shoring equipment shall be installed plumb, level, and true to the dimensions and elevations shown on this drawing.
    *   The entire shoring system must be stable and adequately braced before any concrete placement.
    *   Ensure all connections, pins, and locking devices on shoring frames and post shores are properly engaged and secured.

7.2 **Shoring Frame Assembly:**
    *   Stack 5-foot (5'-0") high frames as required to achieve the necessary shoring height, ensuring proper alignment and secure pin connections between stacked frames.
    *   Install 7-foot (7'-0") bracing diagonally or horizontally between frames to create a rigid and stable tower or wall system. Bracing must be installed at all levels and in both directions to resist lateral loads.
    *   Ensure all frames are equipped with adjustable screw jacks at the base and adjustable U-head plates at the top, as specified.

7.3 **Post Shore Placement:**
    *   Place #2, #3, or #4 post shores precisely at the locations marked with 'X', '[X]', or '&' symbols, respectively, on the shoring plan.
    *   Ensure post shores are plumb and have full bearing on the supporting surface below.
    *   Utilize screw jack base plates at the bottom and U-head plates at the top for fine height adjustment and proper load transfer.
    *   Adjust post shores to the exact required elevation to support the formwork.

7.4 **Joist and Plywood Installation:**
    *   Lay 4x6 wood joists at 19.2 inches on center (O/C) across the U-head plates of the shoring frames and post shores. Ensure joists are level and securely seated within the U-heads.
    *   Place 3/4-inch Douglas Fir #1 plywood decking on top of the joists, ensuring a tight fit and smooth surface for the concrete pour. Secure plywood as necessary to prevent displacement during concrete placement.

7.5 **Adjustable Jack Usage:**
    *   Screw jack base plates and U-head plates are to be used for final height adjustment and to compensate for minor variations in the supporting surface or formwork.
    *   Adjustments should be made carefully to ensure uniform load distribution across all shoring elements. Avoid over-tightening any single jack, which could induce uneven stresses.

7.6 **Contractor-Supplied Elements (Build-Up):**
    *   The Shoring/Forming Contractor (DC Forming Ltd.) is responsible for designing and installing all "BUILD UP UNDER SLAB" and "BUILD UP UNDER SLOPE FOR STAIRS" as required to achieve the specified shoring elevations.
    *   These build-up elements must be structurally sound and capable of safely transferring the shoring loads to the underlying structure or ground. Detailed shop drawings or a specific design by the contractor's engineer may be required for complex build-up scenarios.

7.7 **Specific Shoring Requirements (Slab vs. Slab Band):**
    *   A critical instruction is that **NO SHORE IS REQUIRED UNDER THE TYPICAL 10.5" SLAB NOR UNDER THE 24" SLAB BAND TYPICALLY**, unless specifically indicated on the plan with an 'X', '[X]', or '&' symbol for post shores. This implies that the main shoring frames and joists are primarily supporting the overall slab area, and specific post shores are only needed for localized heavy loads or complex geometry not covered by the general frame layout. The contractor must strictly adhere to this instruction to avoid unnecessary installation or, conversely, missing critical support.

---

### 8.0 SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE

8.1 **Pre-Pour Inspection:**
    *   A mandatory inspection by the undersigned Professional Engineer (P. Eng.) from Greuter Engineering Ltd. is required prior to pouring concrete. This inspection will verify that the shoring system has been installed in full compliance with this drawing, engineering calculations, and all applicable safety standards.
    *   The Shoring/Forming Contractor must provide a minimum of forty-eight (48) hours' notice to the P. Eng. to schedule this inspection. No concrete shall be placed until written approval is received from the P. Eng.

8.2 **Drawing Coordination and Field Verification:**
    *   The Contractor must ensure that all field personnel are familiar with the contents of this drawing and all referenced documents.
    *   Continuous field verification of dimensions, elevations, and material conditions is required throughout the installation process. Any discrepancies or unforeseen conditions must be immediately reported to the P. Eng.

8.3 **Material Usage Restrictions:**
    *   Strict adherence to the restriction on 4x6 wood joist usage (Section 2.4) is paramount for safety. Misuse of these structural members can lead to catastrophic failure of the shoring system.

8.4 **General Safety Practices:**
    *   All work shall be performed in accordance with the latest edition of the Occupational Health and Safety Regulations (OHSR) of British Columbia, Canada, and the Contractor's site-specific safety plan.
    *   Personnel working on or near the shoring system must wear appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).
    *   Proper fall protection measures must be in place during the erection and dismantling of the shoring and formwork.
    *   Access and egress points must be kept clear.
    *   The shoring system must be protected from accidental impact by vehicles or equipment.
    *   Regular inspection of the shoring system for signs of damage, settlement, or instability is required, especially after adverse weather conditions or before concrete placement.

---

### 9.0 ENGINEERING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

9.1 **Professional Engineer's Role:**
    *   Greuter Engineering Ltd., under EGBC Permit No. 1002364, is the Engineer of Record for this shoring design. The P. Eng. is responsible for the overall design integrity and approval of the shoring plan.
    *   The P. Eng. will conduct the pre-pour inspection to confirm compliance with the design.

9.2 **Material Quality Standards:**
    *   All materials, including steel frames, post shores, wood joists, and plywood, must meet or exceed the specifications outlined in Section 5.0.
    *   The Shoring/Forming Contractor is responsible for ensuring that all supplied materials are in good condition, free from damage, corrosion, or defects that could impair their structural performance.
    *   Manufacturer's certifications and data sheets for proprietary shoring equipment (frames, post shores, jacks) shall be available on site for review.
